comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body:
No click needed, and the window that loses the tab is the one that asked for it. Measured on 0.8.1, 2026-09-14, one home (`~/.muster`), two windows: 3742 launched 08:43, and 19284 launched 08:56 with `--fresh`. 19284 had no workspace of its own for 97 minutes - `showing: null`, `regions: []`, `keyboard: null`, `mirror.bootstrap` at 13:56Z and 14:01Z and nothing after.

Then, with the keyboard in 3742 on the CRAB tab:

    15:33:47.686Z  3742   view.region     t22ahb9ayj, keyboard p22k9bcrpv
    15:33:53.577Z  3742   intent          CreateTab { beside: p22k9bcrpv, cwd: /home/src/goat-cr }
    15:33:53.834Z  19284  view.region     t23nf3693h, keyboard p23nf3pw67, tabs 3
    15:33:53.951Z  19284  bridge.start    w6:p1G
    15:33:57.202Z  3742   intent          FocusPane p23nf3pw67
    15:33:59.148Z  3742   intent          FocusPane p23nf3pw67
    15:33:59.391Z  3742   intent          ClosePane p23nf3pw67
    15:33:59.485Z  19284  view.region     t22ahb9ayj
    15:34:00.382Z  19284  bridge.replacing  devenv/p22k9bcrpv

3742 asked for the tab and 19284 drew it. 3742 then asked twice for the keyboard on the pane it had just made, got it neither time, and closed the pane. Twenty seconds later 19284 took the CRAB tab as well - all three panes, `bridge.replacing` on each - and 3742 raised one problem per pane naming `muster pane reattach`.

Two things this adds to the card.

**A tab lands in the window that has nothing, not the window that asked.** `CreateTab` carries `beside: PaneId("p22k9bcrpv")`, and that pane was on screen in 3742, so the request already named where the tab belonged. Nothing had to be guessed. The card's first direction - a tab belongs to one window at a time - covers this if placement reads the intent's own `beside`.

**An empty window is not a harmless one.** 19284 sat there for an hour and a half looking inert, then took the next tab anybody created and the tab the keyboard was on with it. That is the cost of `a_2Mhi0XFTz`'s pane-less window compounding with this card: the window nobody could give a workspace to is the window that takes the next one going.

For anyone hitting it: quit the window that should not have the tab, then `muster pane reattach --pane <each>` in the one that should. Reattaching while both are open works and does not hold, because the next tab or click goes the same way.

creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Every window lists every tab on every machine it is attached to, and since 2026-09-08 every window is attached to both machines: the two-home workaround is retired now that `a_2IZ5TL6DQ` and `a_2I6h18OU6` are done, and `~/.muster/config.toml` names `local` and `devenv`. So "the laptop window" and "the devenv window" are only a convention about which tab each was left on. The laptop window's sidebar shows the devenv agents, and one click on such a row switches that window onto the devenv tab and takes the pane's terminal from the devenv window, which goes dark on it.

Measured on 0.7.0, 2026-09-08, one home, two windows:

- 16:15 the reopened laptop window (pid 41963) restored onto local tab `t20qv2889h`. Between 16:22:50 and 16:23:24 it acquired regions for `t206y99cay` (CRAB) and `t20h22k8pn` (INVESTIGATIONS), both devenv tabs, and was quit showing INVESTIGATIONS. From the keyboard it was indistinguishable from a second devenv window, and that is what it was taken for. Its saved arrangement then pointed at INVESTIGATIONS, so `muster window reopen` would have brought back a devenv-looking window again; `showing` in `state/windows/window-2.toml` was edited by hand first.
- 16:35 after a full quit, `open -a Muster` and then `muster window reopen` both opened onto `t224xeaefr`, the one tab left, because both saved arrangements said so. The second window's bridge took the terminal (`bridge.attach.failed`, then `bridge.replacing`), the first logged `channel.bridge.gone` and drew nothing until `muster pane reattach` was run against it.

`a_2IZPRaJvB` (done) states the experience wanted: "two windows are two independent workspaces rather than two views of one". The tab model (`a_2IoXIHzri`) gave a window an ordered list of tabs and one on screen, but it is the same list in every window. What a window has of its own is its arrangement file, and that records only which tabs it has shown and where the keyboard was in each.

`muster docs limits` already says a second window "opens on tabs of its own" and that the other window's tabs "are still listed and `muster tab focus` still reaches them - what the rule stops is Muster choosing one uninvited". In use the person chooses one uninvited, because nothing marks a tab as another window's.

## Directions, none settled

- **A tab belongs to one window at a time**: the window showing it, or the one that last showed it. Other windows do not list it, or list it greyed and refuse `tab focus` naming the socket that holds it. A tab changes windows by an explicit act, a drag or `muster tab move --window`. This is what makes the sidebar honest and the numbered chords per-window.
- **The arrangement records the window's tab set**, not only the tabs it has shown. That is what lets `reopen` bring a window back onto its own tabs, and what stops two windows opening onto one tab after a quit.
- **A tab made in a window stays in it.** `tab new --daemon` already lands the tab in the asking window; the other window should not list it.

What this costs: the "reach any tab from any window" property, which one client per terminal already makes false in practice; and a tab set is Muster's own record rather than herdr's, which MIP-2 already accepted for cross-machine tabs.

## Validating a fix

- Two windows, one on a laptop tab and one on a devenv tab. Each sidebar shows only its own tabs, or shows the other's unfocusable. Cmd+2 in the laptop window reaches that window's second tab.
- Quit both, relaunch, `muster window reopen`: each window comes back on its own tabs, and no bridge is refused.
- `muster tab move --window` (or a drag) hands a tab across, and the panes in it keep running.
title: 🪟 Two windows are two views of one tab list, and a click in the wrong one steals the pane
